text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Following military ruler General Sani Abacha's order to import fuel to ease an acute shortage in Nigeria, a ship has brought in 40 million litres of petrol to Lagos and two other vessels are expected to dock with fuel by Friday.
- Oil-producing Bayelsa state in the southeast gets a new military administrator, Navy Captain Ominiyi Caleb Olubolade, who replaces ailing Navy Captain Oladipo Ayeni.
- Provisional ruling council to meet in the capital on Wednesday to discuss the transition to civil rule programme.
- Hopes of early respite from the gruelling fuel scarcity bouyed as first consignment of petrol is expected in Lagos.

- Judicial commission investigating ethnic clashes in oil town of Warri urges Shell oil company to initiate and sustain viable projects to tackle perennial conflicts sparked off by feeling of neglect by the people of the area.
- Insurance firms paid out claims amounting to 1.8 billion naira last year, according to a yearly report of the Nigerian insurers assocaition.
- Merger last October of pharmaceutical firms SmithKline and Stirling Products has so far saved 62.5 million naira for the resulting firm, Smithkline Beecham.

- Nigeria lost three billion naira in projected oil revenue from ethnic clashes in oil-producing Warri area which shut Shell oil flow stations there in March, an official of the company told a judicial probe panel on Tuesday.

- Britain will not compromise its stand against human rights violations in Nigeria, says its new high commissioner (ambassador) graham Burton at a meeting in the capital Abuja on Tuesday with a senior Nigerian official.
